items.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I was with a group called Ray Scott, he was a singer, and we had a girl drummer.

ctx.x: Jay and the Americans was one of the headlining groups, and I was with a group called Ray Scott, he was a singer, and we had a girl drummer. And the show toured in Italy on the coastline, all of the resorts down the coast line, Viareggio, we even went to Rome. Then after we left there we ended up in France and — oh right now the name escapes me, but it’s one of the places where they have the festivals in the south of France. And after then I think — oh we ended up in Paris, because we played Salle Pleyel, and…

me a chance to get to Paris. So I left, well the show ended there and I stayed in Paris and I lived over in Montmarte. And I used to take the — well they call it the metro there. So I learned how to use the metro and you’d get all over Paris. And the great thing about the metro, if you knew where you were going you could find it very easily. And so I would go over to the Left Bank. In fact the club I worked in was a club called oh, Le Chat qui Peche, which means a cat with fishes. And the lady who owned the club…
